description: Frontex produces a wide range of communication products to successfully address its large number of stakeholders. The Agency strives to meet the needs and expectations that each specific target audience has, by tailoring content, form and means of distribution accordingly. To achieve success, it is key that the information is shared in a clear, timely and relevant way, meeting the highest professional quality standards. All communication products, regardless of their kind and medium, must be of excellent language quality to strengthen the Agency’s image. Many of the Frontex communication products are drafted and copy-edited in MS Word while the required templates and layouts are usually done or adapted in dedicated layout software such as Adobe InDesign or MS Publisher. Once the layout process is concluded, a significant number of the communication products are checked again towards language correctness and style. The proofreading, editing and writing services are therefore needed on virtually everyday basis – hence the need for the new contract for such services. In addition, the proofreading and editing services are essential for the production of large training and other manuals with long shelf life, and which are shared with EU member states and other key partners, forging the image of Frontex as the agency setting the highest professional standards in border management.

summary: Frontex Surveillance Aircraft Services with long range maritime surveillance fixed wing aircraft
content: Frontex Surveillance Aircraft Services with long range maritime surveillance fixed wing aircraft

caName: Frontex Surveillance Aircraft Services with long range maritime surveillance fixed wing aircraft
description:
Frontex is looking for EU Contractors to provide a fully-fledged service with manned fixed wing aircraft for aerial surveillance over sea which includes:
a. aircraft; b.	sufficient number of crew members (pilot, sensor operator, technician, etc.) in order to be able to deliver minimum 2 flight missions per day without any limitation;  c.	sufficient number of Liaison officer(s) in the assigned Operation Coordination Centre (Host MS ICC or Frontex HQ) during the entire deployment period, who will be working on the tasks related to the flight from 60 minutes before the moment of a take-off to 60 minutes following the landing; d. maintenance capability; e. data transmission capability via BRLOS (including near real time video streaming of the EO/IR) to the Operation Coordination Centre; f. logistical infrastructure and ground support (e.g. hangar, parking place of the aircraft, fuel, etc.); g. administrative responsibility (management of any permissions related to registration, certification, transportation, deployment, authorizations, insurances, permissions to fly, etc.) to deliver aerial surveillance over the external maritime border of the Host Country; h.	the Contractor shall provide the collected data directly from the Asset to the designated Frontex Coordination Centre via BRLOS with a minimum uplink speed of 512 kbps.
The Service which the Contractor shall provide under this FWC is based on mission flights where the Asset, following Frontex instructions, surveys the Area of Interest, included in the Service Deployment Area, searching for ‘objects of interest’ mandated by Frontex Regulation, and passing surveillance data and information to the Operational Coordination Centre designated by Frontex.
Aircraft shall be able:
- to reach the Area of Interest (surveillance area) located at a distance of more than 401NM from the Base Airport and; - deliver minimum 2.5 hours mission flight in the Area of Interest with the average speed as of approximately 150 knots, between 1000 feet and 6000 feet and return back to the base airport and; - to perform a total minimum of 6 hours of flight (excluding final reserve and contingency fuel) with 2 Frontex liaison officers on board in line with the requirements above, with the minimum mandatory Payload.
These missions may also take place over Third Country (TC) waters, TC land territory, as well as to be operated from TC Base Airport. 
The aircraft has an approved life-raft drop capability (each life-raft has at least 10 PAX capacity, on board  the total dropping capacity should secure enough life raft(s) for minimum 30 PAX) and in case of activation of life-raft drop the deployed aircraft can continue its mission flight (without an early landing) and after landing the second mission flight with full operational configuration (including life rafts) may take place within 60 minutes. 
Contracting Authority will consider as advantage the emergency broadcast system on the life raft 406 or 121.5 MHZ.
Optionally, the aircraft can have the drop capability of life buoys able to broadcast minimum their position for at least 48 hours.
The Contractor shall guarantee that the Asset is equipped with the following sensors: 
a.	HD multi-sensor Electro-Optical/ Infrared camera for day and night operations;  b. Automatic Identification System (AIS) receiver; c. Weather detection and avoidance system according to EASA and competent authorities’ prescriptions and certification requirements for the given type of Aircraft, in order to be able to perform all the type of flights requested by the prospective framework contract, following day and night IFR and VFR flight rules; d.	Dedicated Maritime Surveillance Radar: minimum requirement to operate in X band and track minimum 500 simultaneous targets; e. Global navigation satellite system receiver; f.	(Optional) Anti-jamming equipment in GNSS denied environment; g.	Satellite phone.
Duration of the future FWC:  2+2 years

summary: Stationary document readers with warranty, training, and maintenance support
content: Stationary document readers with warranty, training, and maintenance support

caName: Stationary document readers with warranty, training, and maintenance support
description:
The purpose of this Framework Contract is to enhance border checks capabilities through the provision of stationary document readers, accompanied by comprehensive warranty, training, and maintenance support. This acquisition aims to support Frontex's efforts to strengthen border checks and law enforcement cooperation in targeted regions, providing the necessary tools and expertise for effective and efficient operation of document reading systems. All details are specified in the Technical Specifications chapter and Tender Specification document.
Technical capacities of Western Balkan partners to conduct border checks and border surveillance are increased 
The following activities will be implemented under output 2.2: 

2.2.1	Coordination of equipment donation among EU actors and Member States

To avoid overlaps with deliveries of other border management equipment funded by the EU, Frontex will organise regular exchanges at working-level with the Commission, Member States and the EU Delegations on equipment needs, as well as to ensure close coordination of planned supplies. This will be done via regular exchanges, in particular with relevant beneficiaries prior to any equipment being purchased and supplied.

2.2.2	Procurement of technical equipment for border checks

In parallel to the rollout of training, Frontex will, in consultation with its Wester Balkan partners and based on its expertise on state-of-the-art technology, procure technical equipment to improve the border checks’ performance. These might include videoscopes, detectors, portable ID readers and other devices allowing for more efficient check-ups of vehicles, goods and people. The procurement of the equipment will take place at a later stage of the project, after thorough, evidence-based assessment.

Supply of equipment will be closely coordinated with necessary trainings to ensure its proper use, as well as sustainability of the equipment beyond project implementation.

2.2.3	Procurement of technical equipment for border surveillance 

By the same token as for border checks, Frontex will procure equipment for border surveillance. This might include googles, binoculars, infrared cameras, etc. The procurement of the equipment will take place at a later stage of the project, after thorough, evidence-based assessment.

Supply of equipment will be closely coordinated with necessary trainings to ensure its proper use, as well as sustainability of the equipment beyond project implementation.

summary: Maritime analysis tool
content: Maritime analysis tool

caName: Maritime analysis tool
description:
The subject of the contract is a maritime analysis tool to support Frontex’s maritime analysis function by providing capabilities to analyse and derive insights out of ‘big maritime data’. 
The maritime analytics implies the competent use of the system to support the development and implementation of risk profiles as well as to identify and monitor areas used as embarkation or transit points for irregular migration and cross-border crime.
The maritime analytics system should provide a user-friendly interface and include the integration and fusion of data/information from an increased number of sources. In addition, it is requested to enable customized search rules and queries based on specific ship behaviours. The detailed Terms of Reference (ToR) are included in Annex-I. 
According to the Maritime Analysis Tool ToR (see Annex-I), the ‘usability requirements’ are listed as the following functionalities from the risk analysis perspective that the Maritime Analysis Tool should provide to Frontex analysts:
a.	to capture, store and manage global maritime big data, for at least 5 years previous to the query.
b.	to fuse and integrate maritime ’big data’ with vessels’ historical data, for at least 5 years previous to the query.
c.	To allow the export of the query results with the highest available limit - at least 10.000 entries.

summary: Frontex Surveillance Aircraft Services with long range maritime surveillance fixed wing aircraft
content: Frontex Surveillance Aircraft Services with long range maritime surveillance fixed wing aircraft

caName: Frontex Surveillance Aircraft Services with long range maritime surveillance fixed wing aircraft
description:
Frontex is looking for EU Contractors to provide a fully-fledged service with manned fixed wing aircraft for aerial surveillance over sea which includes:
a. aircraft; b.	sufficient number of crew members (pilot, sensor operator, technician, etc.) in order to be able to deliver minimum 2 flight missions per day without any limitation;  c.	sufficient number of Liaison officer(s) in the assigned Operation Coordination Centre (Host MS ICC or Frontex HQ) during the entire deployment period, who will be working on the tasks related to the flight from 60 minutes before the moment of a take-off to 60 minutes following the landing; d. maintenance capability; e. data transmission capability via BRLOS (including near real time video streaming of the EO/IR) to the Operation Coordination Centre; f. logistical infrastructure and ground support (e.g. hangar, parking place of the aircraft, fuel, etc.); g. administrative responsibility (management of any permissions related to registration, certification, transportation, deployment, authorizations, insurances, permissions to fly, etc.) to deliver aerial surveillance over the external maritime border of the Host Country; h.	the Contractor shall provide the collected data directly from the Asset to the designated Frontex Coordination Centre via BRLOS with a minimum uplink speed of 512 kbps.
The Service which the Contractor shall provide under this FWC is based on mission flights where the Asset, following Frontex instructions, surveys the Area of Interest, included in the Service Deployment Area, searching for ‘objects of interest’ mandated by Frontex Regulation, and passing surveillance data and information to the Operational Coordination Centre designated by Frontex.
Aircraft shall be able:
- to reach the Area of Interest (surveillance area) located at a distance of more than 401NM from the Base Airport and; - deliver minimum 2.5 hours mission flight in the Area of Interest with the average speed as of approximately 150 knots, between 1000 feet and 6000 feet and return back to the base airport and; - to perform a total minimum of 6 hours of flight (excluding final reserve and contingency fuel) with 2 Frontex liaison officers on board in line with the requirements above, with the minimum mandatory Payload.
These missions may also take place over Third Country (TC) waters, TC land territory, as well as to be operated from TC Base Airport. 
The aircraft has an approved life-raft drop capability (each life-raft has at least 10 PAX capacity, on board  the total dropping capacity should secure enough life raft(s) for minimum 30 PAX) and in case of activation of life-raft drop the deployed aircraft can continue its mission flight (without an early landing) and after landing the second mission flight with full operational configuration (including life rafts) may take place within 60 minutes. 
Contracting Authority will consider as advantage the emergency broadcast system on the life raft 406 or 121.5 MHZ.

summary: Shipborne VTOL UAS deployment with data fusion and integration services
content: Shipborne VTOL UAS deployment with data fusion and integration services

caName: Shipborne VTOL UAS deployment with data fusion and integration services
description:
The surveillance of the EU’s land and sea borders is a fundamental component of the European integrated Border Management (EIBM) as identified by the Multiannual Strategic Policy for EIBM 2023-2027 . Border surveillance requires effective operational measures taken by Frontex and Member States’ border management authorities. The Technical and Operational Strategy for EIBM states that these measures should be intelligence-driven and risk-based, drawing on multi-domain sensor networks.  
The multipurpose surveillance-oriented approach, as described in the Capability Roadmap of the EBCG , will require the deployment of integrated, interoperable and inter-connected capabilities that will enable persistent border surveillance, including unmanned systems such as UAS and satellites.
Integrated solution for border surveillance combining shipborne Unmanned Aircraft Systems (UAS) with Vertical Take-off and Landing (VTOL) with data fusion and integration from additional sources has the objective to provide an enhanced level of detail and accuracy in understanding border activity, thereby enabling more effective surveillance and response.
Based on operational capability requirements and previous research efforts, through this Pilot Project the Agency intends to continue evaluating unmanned systems technologies and their capabilities in delivering integrated aerial maritime surveillance, while assessing operational performance, cost-efficiency, and reliability.

content: Delivery of highly specialized training for detecting and combatting the document and identity fraud and associated services.

caName: Delivery of highly specialized training for detecting and combatting the document and identity fraud and associated services.
description:
The services to be provided by the Contractor are the following: 
- TASK 1 Deliver and provide logistics, specialised equipment and relevant learning materials for the Advanced Level Document Officer Course 
- TASK 2 Deliver and provide logistics, specialised equipment and relevant learning materials for the European Course for Specialists on Identity and Security Documents 
- TASK 3 Support development of the session plans for the European Course for Specialists on Identity and Security Documents 

The ALDO course provides the knowledge and the skills to identify genuine documents on the basis of primary and advanced security features and personalisation techniques and to refer suspicious documents to a higher level of expertise. Learners are expected to establish conclusively the status of the document under inspection/examination. The Advanced Level Document Officer course also adds an extra focus on latest technologies and perspectives in authentication of identities, documents and identity fraud.
The CSID course is entirely based on the latest developments of authentication processes in the identity chain, including international dimension with possible international stakeholders. Following the release of the EU strategy on voluntary return and reintegration and the enhanced Frontex
mandate in the area of return and reintegration and also the need to support the Member States in growing
their outreach capacity to the digital space, there is an opportunity to develop the Frontex Return and
Reintegration IT tool composed of a mobile application available in iOS and Android App Stores together
with mirror website, aimed at the users from general public and internal-FX content management module,
referred as the Solution, Main Product or RRApp within confines of this document. 
Currently, there is no Frontex tool in place that comply with the requirements pursued by the Solution
like providing content about Joint Reintegration Services and Frontex Reintegration Programme, displaying
locations of reintegration centres on map, and giving opportunity to have conversation. This fact, added
to the absence of any interrelation or integration with other systems or databases, justify the convenience
to develop the Solution from scratch.

The main aim of the Return and Reintegration Application Solution (hereinafter referred to as ‘RRApp’) is
to provide the information on national return and reintegration programmes of the Member States
transited by potential returnees and by doing this, the potential returnees themselves would benefit from
receiving precise and complete information about the possibility to return to their country of return and
receive reintegration assistance. 
By launching RRApp targeting potential returnees, Frontex adds another tool to the toolbox to assist the
Member States in increasing the number of voluntary returns and uptake of reintegration by: 
• Raising awareness about Assisted Voluntary Return and Reintegration packages;
• Providing information about return and reintegration programmes;
• Providing guidance on reaching the nearest counselling centre;
• Giving ownership of the return and reintegration process to the migrants.
Expected Return and Reintegration Application outcomes are focused on providing a service to the general
public, specifically to migrants interested to participate in voluntary returns and reintegration processes.

content: Remotely Piloted Aircraft System (Medium Altitude Long Endurance) for Maritime Surveillance Services

caName: Remotely Piloted Aircraft System (Medium Altitude Long Endurance) for Maritime Surveillance Services
description:
The provision of a fully-fledged service with unmanned fixed wing aircraft for aerial surveillance over sea which includes: a.	aircraft; b.	sufficient number of crew (pilot, sensor operator, technician, etc.) in order to be able to deliver not less than 80 scheduled mission flight hour within any 168 hours and with minimum 7 hours between the scheduled flights;  c.	sufficient number of Liaison officer(s) in the assigned Operation Coordination Centre (within Host MS or within Frontex HQ) during the entire deployment period, from 60 minutes before the moment of take-off ad 60 minutes following the landing; d.	maintenance capability; e.	data transmission capability via BRLOS (including near real time video streaming of the EO/IR) to the Operation Coordination Centre; f.	logistical infrastructure and ground support (e.g. hangar, parking place of the aircraft, fuel, etc.);  g.	administrative responsibility (including management of any permissions related to registration, transportation, deployment, authorizations, insurances, permissions to fly and any other administrative documents, etc. necessary to deliver aerial surveillance over the external maritime borders of the Host Country; h.	the Contractor shall provide the collected data directly from the Asset to the designated Frontex Coordination Centre via BRLOS with a minimum uplink speed of 320 kbps. 

The Service which the Contractor shall provide under this FWC is based on mission flights where the Asset, following Frontex instructions, surveys the Area of Interest, included in the Service Deployment Area, searching for ‘objects of interest’ mandated by Frontex Regulation, and passing surveillance data and information to the Operational Coordination Centre designated by Frontex.

Aircraft shall be able: a) to reach the Area of Interest (surveillance area) located at a distance of more than 200 kms from the Base Airport and; b) stay 12 hours in the Area of Interest with the average speed as of 60 knots, between 2500 feet and 4500 feet and return back to the base airport and; c) to perform a total minimum of 18 hours of flight (excluding final reserve and contingency fuel) in line with the 2 requirements above with the minimum mandatory Payload stipulated in the Tender Dossier.

The Contractor shall guarantee that the Asset is equipped with the following sensors: a.	Electro-Optical/ Infrared camera with the following capacity (i. giro – stabilized turret; ii.  thermal imager; iii. daylight zoom camera) b. AIS receiver; c. Dedicated maritime surveillance radar; d. Global navigation satellite system receiver.

Host Countries of the base airports: Malta or Italy or Greece with no relocation during the implementation of the Specific Orders.

The Contractor shall guarantee that all Contractor’s personnel (crew/staff) involved in the management of data/ information is having valid EU MS security clearance, at the minimum level of CONFIDENTIEL UE/EU CONFIDENTIAL (the declaration of possession/processing/intention of applying for, after FWC signature, of such security clearances by the relevant personnel shall be stated in the Contractor’s offer for the FWC).

Tender is open only for EU companies and EU companies with subcontractors from third countries.
